You spent years perfecting the craft. Your website got one weekend and a free template.

Here's the thing nobody tells you: a new client sees your site before they see your work. If it's slow, broken, or still has "Lorem ipsum" in the footer, they don't think "she's busy." They think "sketchy."

Your talent is not the problem. The front door is.

Start with the $200 teardown. Link in bio.

QUICK QUESTION
When did you last update your website?
THIS YEAR
WHAT WEBSITE?
Next frame: share the results with "I knew it." and a link sticker to the teardown.
A free template from 2017? For your signature work? Groundbreaking. Dress the front door. Link in bio — $200 teardown.

Hi. I'm Makayla, the founder of No Empty Chair.

I spent years in TV news making short videos people actually stop scrolling for. Two Emmy nominations, a Murrow Award, and a lot of 4 a.m. edits later, I noticed something: the most talented people I knew (my stylist, my braider, my barber) had the worst online front doors.

So I built a studio for them. Branding, websites and short-form content made to fill chairs, not rack up likes.

If your work is a ten and your calendar isn't, we should talk. Every project starts with the $200 teardown.

#noemptychair #atlantabeauty #salonmarketing #womeninbusiness #atlantaentrepreneur

Sun · Oct 4 · QUESTION BOX
SUNDAY QUESTION
What's the one question clients DM you the most?
TELL ME
Answer 3 to 5 during the week as stories with "that belongs on your website." Easy content, warm leads.

Nine thousand people watch you. Three of them paid you this week.

That's not a following problem. That's a front door problem. Somewhere between "love this!!" and "booked," people are getting lost: no prices, a dead link, a DM that never got answered.

Views are nice. Bookings pay rent. Let's build the part that pays.

The $200 teardown is a short video showing the three fixes that turn the followers you already have into bookings. Link in bio.

#beautybusiness #salonmarketing #instagramforbusiness #atlbraider #atlnails
Views are a vibe. Bookings are a business. If your follower count and your calendar don't match, the problem is what happens after they tap your profile.

A booking site does four things: shows the price, shows open times, takes the deposit, gets the policy signed. This is what that looks like. Clients don't want to ask. They want to book. Link in bio for the $200 teardown.

Wed · Oct 7 · SLIDER
THE HANDS PROBLEM
How much of your week is spent on things that aren't the actual service?
BARELYALL OF IT
Primes Thursday's carousel (F03). Share results Thursday morning.

Quick question: if you broke your wrist tomorrow, how long until the money stops?

If the answer is "immediately," you don't have a business yet. You have a very skilled job with a ring light.

That's not a shame thing. It's a setup thing. When your page shows the prices, answers the questions, and sends people straight to book, your hands can stay on the hair.

Save this. Then send it to the friend who answered "how much?" 40 times today.

Start with the $200 teardown. Link in bio.

#salonowner #beautybusiness #businesssystems #atlantasalon #salonmarketing
Not trying to scare you. Okay, a little. Your talent deserves a business that doesn't depend on you being in the chair 60 hours a week.

Fri · Oct 9 · THIS OR THAT
YOU ONLY GET ONE
100K followers, or a booked-out month?
FOLLOWERS
BOOKINGS
Follow-up frame: "Then post like it." Primes F05.
By all means, keep sending prices by DM. Your competitors adore it. Put the price on the page. Link in bio — $200 teardown.

Every "you available?" DM is a sign, and it's not that clients are annoying.

It means your availability, prices and policies are hiding. So people ask. Then they ghost. Then you post a rant about time-wasters.

A good booking page answers three things before anyone messages you: what you do, what it costs, and when you're free. One tap to book. No back-and-forth.

Your DMs should be for regulars saying thank you, not strangers asking for your calendar.

#salonowner #bookingsystem #braiderlife #atlantahairstylist #beautypreneur
"How much for knotless?" Asked all day, booked far less. Every style, length and price listed. Pick a time, pay the deposit, done. Your price isn't a secret. It's a filter. Link in bio.

"I'm booked for three months" hits different when you haven't had a Saturday off since 2022.

Here's the thing: a waitlist is your clients telling you you're underpriced. But raising rates is scary when your page still looks like a $60 shop.

Premium work needs a premium front door. When the brand looks the part, the new price doesn't need explaining.

Tell me in the comments: when did you last raise your prices?

#salonlife #raiseyourrates #beautybusiness #stylistlife #salonowner
I'm sweet to people. I am not sweet to websites. Which line hit a little too close? Be honest.

A no-show on a Saturday is rent you don't get back. The fix: a deposit at checkout, a clear reschedule window, fine print people actually read, a policy they tick. Systems protect you. Rants don't. Link in bio.

Wed · Oct 14 · QUIZ
POP QUIZ
Which one is an actual booking system?
A · My DMs
B · My Notes app
C · A page that takes deposits
D · My cousin
Correct answer: C. Reshare results with "If you picked D, we need to talk."

I make short-form video for a living (2x Emmy-nominated), so hear me: content matters. But somewhere along the way, a lot of us started performing for the algorithm instead of building for the client.

Your next client doesn't care about your morning routine. She cares whether you can do her lash fill by Friday, what it costs, and where to click.

Be both if you want. Just make sure the business half actually has a booking button.

Which column are you in right now? Be honest in the comments.

#lashtech #beautyinfluencer #beautybusiness #contentcreator #salonmarketing
The brand deal is a bonus. The client who rebooks every six weeks is the business. Make your page for her.

You've seen the post. Maybe you've made the post. Four paragraphs of policies in a screenshot, all caps, three colors.

Here's the truth: nobody reads it. Not because clients are rude, but because a caption is the wrong place for a contract.

Deposits, lateness, add-ons, cancellations: all of it belongs inside your booking flow, with a checkbox. Agreed to before they pay. Enforced without you arguing in the comments.

Protect your time with systems, not paragraphs.

#salonpolicies #bookingpolicy #braider #lashtech #salonowner
What a client needs to say yes: the cost, how long it takes, what to expect, one button to book. Your vibe is the product. Your site should feel like it. Link in bio.

Be honest, how many of these are running your calendar right now?

No judgment. Most of the best artists I know started exactly here. But every booking that lives in your head is a booking you can lose, double up, or forget to confirm.

A real booking page (Square, StyleSeat, Booksy, whatever you use), built into a site that looks like your work, takes deposits and books clients while you're mid-install.

Tag the friend with 14 links in her Linktree.

Nobody reads your whole bio. They scan it, feel something, and decide. Make sure what they feel is "I need to book her."

Wed · Oct 21 · POLL
THE HANDS PROBLEM
Could you take two weeks off without losing money?
YES, I'M BUILT
LOL. NO.
Primes Thursday's "Your hands are not a retirement plan" (F07).

Wrists, backs, knees. Ask any braider over 35 what 10 years behind the chair costs.

The goal was never to do every head yourself forever. The goal is a brand strong enough to book an assistant, sell a class, fill a second chair, or take a month off without the calendar going quiet.

That starts with how you show up online. A brand that only works when you're in the photo can't grow past you.

Save this. Your future wrists will thank you.

Count how many jobs you did today that weren't the actual service. The first one I'd take off your plate: answering the same five questions in your DMs.

Fri · Oct 23 · RESHARE BAIT
RESHARE IF
You've answered "how much?" forty times today.
And every single one of them left you on read.
No sticker. Built to be reshared into other pros' stories.
"Booked and busy," darling? The link is broken. Let's fix that. Link in bio — $200 teardown.

"Can you do it for less?" isn't only about the client. It's about what your page told them before they asked.

Blurry flyer, no prices listed, a booking link that's a Google Form? That reads as negotiable.

Clean branding, clear prices, real reviews and a smooth checkout read as "this is her rate." People don't haggle with a business that looks like one.

Your price is your price. Make your brand say it for you.

Simple. Short-form is my whole career. I've spent years figuring out what makes someone stop, watch and act in under three seconds, for millions of viewers.

Your clients are scrolling the same feed. The difference between a view and a booking is the hook, the pacing and one clear next step.

That's what I bring to your page. Not trends. Strategy.
